items.abstract:
<jats:title>A<jats:sc>bstract</jats:sc>
          </jats:title>
          <jats:p>The transverse part of the vector-axial vector flavor current correlator in the presence of weak external electric field is studied using holography. The correlator is calculated using a bottom-up model <jats:ext-link xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xlink:href="http://arxiv.org/abs/arXiv:1003.2377" ext-link-type="uri">proposed recently</jats:ext-link>, that includes both contributions of higher string states and the non-linear dynamics of the chiral condensate. It is shown that for low momenta the result agrees with the relation proposed by <jats:ext-link xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xlink:href="http://arxiv.org/abs/arXiv:1010.0718" ext-link-type="uri">Son and Yamamoto</jats:ext-link> motivated by a simpler holographic model. This suggests that the Son-Yamamoto relation is generically valid in the IR of models with the proper chiral symmetry breaking pattern.</jats:p>
title: Vector-axial vector correlators in weak electric field and the holographic dynamics of the chiral condensate

items.abstract: <jats:p>Three methods of perturbing the ground state of the He4 dimer by electric fields are treated: the Stark shift by large static electric fields; dissociation by a pulsed electric field; and the coupling of a plane wave to the interaction-induced quadrupole moment of the dimer. The second process, with coupling to the interaction-induced polarizability anisotropy of the dimer, appears to offer the best prospect for observable perturbation of the dimer. The estimates are based on results of ab initio calculations of properties of the He–He system.</jats:p>
title: Electric field effects on the helium dimer
